cards.title: Urea Dilution Correction for Lavage-Derived Epithelial Lining Fluid Concentrations
cards.claim: Under the urea dilution method, apparent ELF volume is V_ELF = V_BALF × U_BALF / U_plasma and apparent analyte concentration is C_ELF = C_BALF × U_plasma / U_BALF. Urea concentrations must use the same units; the corrected analyte concentration retains the units of C_BALF. The result is a dilution-corrected concentration, not a direct measurement of unbound or active exposure.
conditions: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and the blood reference are paired to the same animal and sampling occasion.
The protocol qualifies urea as a dilution marker under its collection conditions.
The urea denominator is measured and quantifiable; an absent or invalid denominator prevents numerical correction.
required_inputs: Measured analyte concentration in BALF with calibration, assay limits and analyte basis.
Paired BALF and plasma urea concentrations with matching units and assay provenance.
Recovered lavage volume when V_ELF is needed; sample identifiers and collection times.
limitations: Marker equilibration and collection conditions affect interpretation.
The formula does not identify binding, intracellular exposure or pharmacological activity.
Do not substitute zero for BLQ values or import a universal assay limit/outlier threshold from the cited study.
cards.downstream_use: Produce a traceable apparent ELF concentration for site-exposure analysis while retaining the raw BALF and urea measurements.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
